definition_en: to become firm or solid, or to become less gentle and more severe
core_image: 湿润的泥巴在太阳下慢慢干裂发硬
scene: 冷风让泥土变硬了。The cold wind hardened the soil.
sceneCN: 这里 harden 是「使变硬」（第 1 个义项）；句意：冷风让泥土变硬了。

senses.title: Become solid
senses.definition: to become firm and solid
senses.definitionCN: 变得坚实而坚硬
senses.example: The cold wind hardened the soil.
senses.exampleCN: 冷风让泥土变硬了。
senses.why: This is the material sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是材料层面的义项。

senses.title: Become strong
senses.definition: to make a person strong enough to face difficulty
senses.definitionCN: 使人坚强到足以面对困难
senses.example: The years had hardened him.
senses.exampleCN: 岁月让他变得坚强。
senses.why: Hard material became a hard character.
senses.whyCN: 坚硬的材料，变成了坚硬的性格。

senses.title: Become severe
senses.definition: to make an attitude or rule less gentle
senses.definitionCN: 使态度或规定变得不再宽和
senses.example: Their attitude hardened after the attack.
senses.exampleCN: 那次袭击之后，他们的态度变强硬了。
senses.why: Strength in the wrong place becomes severity.
senses.whyCN: 用错地方的坚强，就成了严厉。

intro.en: Harden is hard plus the verb ending -en, formed in Middle English.
intro.cn: harden 是 hard 加动词词尾 -en，在中古英语中构成。

items.en: Heard meant firm.
items.cn: heard 意为坚实。

items.en: Harden meant to make firm.
items.cn: harden 意为使变硬。

items.en: It described clay, metal, and cement.
items.cn: 它描述黏土、金属与水泥。

items.en: The sense moved to hardened people.
items.cn: 词义扩展到变得坚强的人。

items.en: It also named hardened attitudes.
items.cn: 它也指变得强硬的态度。

note.en: Harden is compared with look-alike words and with words for becoming firm.
note.cn: 把 harden 与形近词以及表示变坚硬的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Harden turns soft clay into stone, and a soft heart into something that can bear the cold.
normalIntro.cn: harden 把软泥变成石头，也把柔软的心变成能抗住寒冷的东西。

normal.en: The cement hardened in a day.
Frost hardened the ground.
He hardened his heart against pity.
Their views hardened over time.
normal.cn: 随着时间推移，他们的看法变得强硬。

normal.en: Training hardened the team.

abstract.en: What one hardens can no longer bend.
abstract.cn: 被弄硬的东西，就再也弯不了了。

abstract.en: A hardened heart is a wall with no door.
abstract.cn: 变硬的心，是一堵没有门的墙。

abstract.en: Strength is a good servant and a bad master.
abstract.cn: 坚强是好仆人，却是坏主人。

examples.en: The cold wind hardened the soil.
The years had hardened him.
Their attitude hardened after the attack.
examples.cn: 那次袭击之后，他们的态度变强硬了。

dict_mnemonic.text: harden 是 hard 加 -en，指「使变硬、变硬」，如水泥凝固；也可指人「变得坚强」或态度「变得强硬」，harden the heart 是铁了心。

root: hard（硬的）加动词后缀 -en；由物质变硬，引申为人变得坚强，以及态度、规定变得严厉强硬。

sensesIntro.en: Harden means to turn soft material solid, a soft person strong, or a mild attitude severe.
sensesIntro.cn: harden 指让软材料变硬、让柔软的人变强，或让温和的态度变严厉。

core.en: Wet clay drying into a hard shape.
core.cn: 湿黏土干成坚硬的形状。

branches.en: Frost turns mud into stone.
branches.cn: 霜把泥变成石头。

branches.en: A worker carries more each year.
branches.cn: 一个工人每年承担得更多。

branches.en: A rule becomes stricter after one mistake.
branches.cn: 一次失误后，规定变得严格。

branches.en: The ground and the spirit both test the frost.
branches.cn: 土地与精神，都要经受霜冻的检验。

branches.en: A strength that closes becomes a hardness.
branches.cn: 封闭起来的坚强，就成了冷酷。

intro.en: Harden follows the -en pattern of verbs from adjectives.
intro.cn: harden 遵循「形容词加 -en 变动词」的模式。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root; the word is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词根，属于日耳曼语来源。

definition_en: almost not at all, or only just
core_image: 一束几乎看不见的微光
scene: 他几乎听不见她的声音。He could hardly hear her voice.
sceneCN: 这里 hardly 是「几乎不」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他几乎听不见她的声音。

senses.title: Almost not
senses.definition: to almost no degree at all
senses.definitionCN: 程度几乎为零
senses.example: He could hardly hear her voice.
senses.exampleCN: 他几乎听不见她的声音。
senses.why: This is the main modern sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是现代最主要的意思。

senses.title: Surely not
senses.definition: used to say that something is very unlikely or unsuitable
senses.definitionCN: 用于表示某事极不可能或不合适
senses.example: That is hardly a fair answer.
senses.exampleCN: 那简直算不上公平的回答。
senses.why: The same smallness turns into doubt.
senses.whyCN: 同样的「极少」，转成了怀疑。

senses.title: Only just
senses.definition: only a moment ago
senses.definitionCN: 只在片刻之前
senses.example: I had hardly arrived when it rained.
senses.exampleCN: 我刚到就下雨了。
senses.why: An older sense of barely in time.
senses.whyCN: 这是「时间上刚好」的古老义项。

intro.en: Hardly is hard plus -ly, which first meant with force and later almost not.
intro.cn: hardly 是 hard 加 -ly，最初意为「用力地」，后转为「几乎不」。

items.en: Heard meant firm.
items.cn: heard 意为坚实。

items.en: Hardly meant with force.
items.cn: hardly 意为用力地。

items.en: The sense shifted to barely.
items.cn: 词义转向「勉强、几乎不」。

items.en: Hardly ever became a common phrase.
items.cn: hardly ever 成为常用搭配。

items.en: Hardly also marked things almost untrue.
items.cn: hardly 也用来表示「简直不」。

note.en: Hardly is compared with look-alike words and with words of small degree.
note.cn: 把 hardly 与形近词以及表示微小程度的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Hardly looks like hard but means almost not, a small light on the edge of seeing.
normalIntro.cn: hardly 看着像 hard，意思却是「几乎不」，像视野边缘的一点微光。

normal.en: I can hardly believe it.
She hardly eats meat.
He hardly ever calls.
There is hardly any water left.
I had hardly sat down when the phone rang.

abstract.en: What is hardly there still asks to be noticed.
abstract.cn: 几乎不存在的东西，仍然渴望被看见。

abstract.en: Hard work and hardly working are a letter apart.
abstract.cn: 努力工作与几乎不做，只差一个字母。

abstract.en: Almost nothing is still something.
abstract.cn: 几乎什么都没有，也还是有一点。

examples.en: He could hardly hear her voice.
examples.cn: 他几乎听不见她的声音。

examples.en: That is hardly a fair answer.
examples.cn: 那简直算不上公平的回答。

examples.en: I had hardly arrived when it rained.

dict_mnemonic.text: hardly 虽是 hard 加 -ly，意思却不是「努力地」，而是「几乎不」；hardly ever 是几乎从不，hardly any 是几乎没有，hardly...when 是刚一……就。

root: hard（用力、艰难）加 -ly；中古英语本指「用力地」，后词义转为「勉强、几乎不」与「简直不」。

sensesIntro.en: Hardly means almost not, surely not, or only just.
sensesIntro.cn: hardly 指几乎不、简直不，或刚刚才。

core.en: A light too faint to be sure of.
core.cn: 弱得让人不敢确定的一点光。

branches.en: A voice fades at the far end of a hall.
branches.cn: 声音在走廊尽头淡去。

branches.en: An excuse does not hold up.
branches.cn: 一个借口站不住脚。

branches.en: A door closes just as a knock comes.
branches.cn: 门刚关上，敲门声就响了。

branches.en: What is almost nothing is also almost untrue.
branches.cn: 几乎为零的东西，也几乎不成立。

branches.en: A bare moment is a small amount of time.
branches.cn: 「刚刚」不过是极少的一点时间。

intro.en: Hardly is fixed in form, built from hard and -ly.
intro.cn: hardly 形式固定，由 hard 与 -ly 构成。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root; the word is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词根，属于日耳曼语来源。

items.example: Test the hardness of the stone.

definition_en: causing harm or damage
core_image: 一缕黑烟正飘向窗内的绿植
scene: 过强的阳光对皮肤有害。Too much sun is harmful to the skin.
sceneCN: 这里 harmful 是「有害的」（第 1 个义项）；句意：过强的阳光对皮肤有害。

senses.title: Bad for the body
senses.definition: likely to damage a person's health
senses.definitionCN: 很可能损害人的健康
senses.example: Too much sun is harmful to the skin.
senses.exampleCN: 过强的阳光对皮肤有害。
senses.why: This is the health sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是健康层面的义项。

senses.title: Bad for nature
senses.definition: likely to damage the natural world
senses.definitionCN: 很可能破坏自然环境
senses.example: These gases are harmful to the environment.
senses.exampleCN: 这些气体对环境有害。
senses.why: The same damage aimed at a larger body.
senses.whyCN: 同样的损害，指向更大的身体。

senses.title: Bad for a person's good
senses.definition: likely to damage a person's development or judgement
senses.definitionCN: 很可能损害人的成长或判断
senses.example: Such advice can be harmful to a child.
senses.exampleCN: 这样的建议可能对孩子有害。
senses.why: The effect sense reaches beyond the body.
senses.whyCN: 影响层面的义项超出身体之外。

intro.en: Harmful is harm plus the adjective ending -ful, meaning full of.
intro.cn: harmful 是 harm 加形容词后缀 -ful，意为「充满……的」。

items.en: Hearm meant injury.
items.cn: hearm 意为伤害。

items.en: The ending -ful meant full of.
items.cn: 后缀 -ful 意为充满。

items.en: Harmful named what brings injury.
items.cn: harmful 指带来伤害的东西。

items.en: It spread to chemicals and habits.
items.cn: 它扩展到化学物质与习惯。

items.en: It also described effects on nature.
items.cn: 它也描述对自然的影响。

note.en: Harmful is compared with look-alike words and with words for causing damage.
note.cn: 把 harmful 与形近词以及表示造成损害的形容词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Harmful is a thing full of harm, whether it touches skin, air, or a young mind.
normalIntro.cn: harmful 就是装满伤害的东西，不论它碰到的是皮肤、空气，还是年幼的心。

normal.en: Smoking is harmful to health.
Plastic waste is harmful to fish.
Some insects are harmful to crops.
The drug has harmful effects.
normal.cn: 这种药有有害的副作用。

normal.en: Too much noise is harmful.

abstract.en: What helps one thing may be harmful to another.
abstract.cn: 对一物有益的，可能对另一物有害。

abstract.en: The most harmful things often arrive quietly.
abstract.cn: 最有害的东西，往往悄悄地来。

abstract.en: To know what harms is the first form of care.
abstract.cn: 知道什么有害，是关心的第一步。

examples.en: Too much sun is harmful to the skin.
examples.cn: 过强的阳光对皮肤有害。

examples.en: These gases are harmful to the environment.
Such advice can be harmful to a child.
examples.cn: 这样的建议可能对孩子有害。

dict_mnemonic.text: harmful 是 harm 加 -ful，意为「有害的」，常用结构 be harmful to；说吸烟有害健康用 harmful to health，说塑料有害环境用 harmful to the environment。

root: harm（伤害）加形容词后缀 -ful（充满……的）；指容易造成身体、环境或成长方面损害的。

sensesIntro.en: Harmful means likely to damage health, the environment, or a person's good.
sensesIntro.cn: harmful 指容易损害健康、环境，或一个人的成长。

core.en: A thing that carries harm inside it.
core.cn: 一个自身携带着伤害的东西。

branches.en: Smoke reaches a pair of lungs.
branches.cn: 烟进入双肺。

branches.en: Waste water flows into a river.
branches.cn: 废水流入河流。

branches.en: A cruel word shapes a small mind.
branches.cn: 一句刻薄的话塑造了一颗小心灵。

branches.en: The same substance can hurt a body and a river.
branches.cn: 同一种物质，能伤害身体与河流。

branches.en: What pollutes the world also pollutes the young.
branches.cn: 污染世界的东西，也污染孩子。

intro.en: Harmful takes more and most and builds a noun and an adverb.
intro.cn: harmful 用 more 与 most 构成比较，并派生名词与副词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root; the word is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词根，属于日耳曼语来源。

items.example: They tested the harmfulness of the gas.
items.exampleCN: 他们检测了这种气体的有害性。

items.example: The dust is harmful to health.

definition_en: a pleasing combination of sounds, or a peaceful and balanced relationship
core_image: 几把不同的乐器同时奏出同一个和弦
scene: 几个声部合在一起很和谐。The voices blended in harmony.
sceneCN: 这里 harmony 是「和谐」（第 1 个义项）；句意：几个声部合在一起很和谐。

senses.title: Pleasing sound
senses.definition: a combination of musical notes that sounds pleasant together
senses.definitionCN: 同时发声而听起来悦耳的音符组合
senses.example: The voices blended in harmony.
senses.exampleCN: 几个声部合在一起很和谐。
senses.why: This is the musical origin sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是源自音乐的义项。

senses.title: Things fitting together
senses.definition: a state in which different parts fit well together
senses.definitionCN: 不同部分彼此契合的状态
senses.example: The colours are in harmony.
senses.exampleCN: 这些颜色很协调。
senses.why: Pleasing notes became pleasing parts.
senses.whyCN: 悦耳的音，变成了悦目的搭配。

senses.title: Peace between people
senses.definition: a peaceful relationship without fighting
senses.definitionCN: 没有争斗的和平关系
senses.example: The two families live in harmony.
senses.exampleCN: 两家人和睦相处。
senses.why: Parts that fit in sound also fit in society.
senses.whyCN: 声音里契合的部分，也能在社会里契合。

intro.en: Harmony comes from Greek harmonia, a joining together.
intro.cn: harmony 来自希腊语 harmonia，意为连接、结合。

items.en: Harmonia meant a fitting together.
items.cn: harmonia 意为契合连接。

items.en: Harmonia entered Latin as harmony of sound.
items.cn: harmonia 在拉丁语中指声音的和谐。

items.en: The word reached English through French.
items.cn: 这个词经由法语进入英语。

items.en: Harmony named music and then agreement.
items.cn: harmony 先指音乐，后指一致。

items.en: It came to mean peace among people.
items.cn: 它进而指人与人之间的和睦。

note.en: Harmony is compared with look-alike words and with words for agreement and peace.
note.cn: 把 harmony 与形近词以及表示一致和和平的词作比较。

entries.definition: the state of having the same view

normalIntro.en: Harmony began as notes that fit and became people who fit.
normalIntro.cn: harmony 起初是彼此相合的音，后来成了彼此相合的人。

normal.en: The choir sang in harmony.
The garden is in harmony with the house.
They lived in harmony for years.
We must work in harmony.
normal.cn: 我们必须协调一致地工作。

normal.en: Peace and harmony returned to the town.
normal.cn: 和平与和睦回到了小镇。

abstract.en: Harmony is difference that has agreed to cooperate.
abstract.cn: 和谐，是差异同意合作。

abstract.en: One voice alone has no harmony to offer.
abstract.cn: 单独一个声音，给不出和声。

abstract.en: The sweetest sound is many sounds that do not fight.
abstract.cn: 最甜的声音，是许多不打架的声音。

examples.en: The voices blended in harmony.
examples.cn: 几个声部合在一起很和谐。

examples.en: The colours are in harmony.
The two families live in harmony.

dict_mnemonic.text: harmony 来自希腊语「连接」，先指声音的「和声、和谐」，再指颜色的「协调」与人际的「和睦」；in harmony with 是与……和谐一致。

root: 希腊语 harmonia（契合、连接）经拉丁语与法语进入英语；由和声的悦耳，引申为部分之间的协调与人际的和睦。

sensesIntro.en: Harmony is notes that sound well, parts that fit well, or people who live well together.
sensesIntro.cn: harmony 是悦耳的音、契合的部分，或和睦相处的人。

core.en: Two notes that meet and do not clash.
core.cn: 两个相遇而不冲突的音。

branches.en: A choir holds one long chord.
branches.cn: 合唱团保持一个长和弦。

branches.en: Curtains and walls share one colour.
branches.cn: 窗帘与墙共享一种颜色。

branches.en: Two neighbours share a fence and a meal.
branches.cn: 两家邻居共用一道篱笆和一餐饭。

branches.en: Sound and sight can both be tuned.
branches.cn: 声音与视觉，都能被调准。

branches.en: Things that fit make people who fit.
branches.cn: 彼此契合的东西，造就彼此契合的人。

intro.en: Harmony builds adjectives with -ious and a verb with -ize.
intro.cn: harmony 加 -ious 构成形容词，加 -ize 构成动词。

latinIntro.en: The Greek base harmonia means a joining.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊词基 harmonia 意为连接。

items.example: The room is full of harmony.

items.exampleCN: 他们把两个方案协调起来。

definition_en: the straps and bands used to control a horse, or to control and use a force
core_image: 皮带与铜扣把一匹马稳稳系在车辕上
scene: 农民给马套上马具。The farmer put the harness on the horse.
sceneCN: 这里 harness 是「马具」（第 1 个义项）；句意：农民给马套上马具。

senses.title: Straps for an animal
senses.definition: the set of straps used to tie an animal to a cart or plough
senses.definitionCN: 把牲畜系在车或犁上的一套皮带
senses.example: The farmer put the harness on the horse.
senses.exampleCN: 农民给马套上马具。
senses.why: This is the basic object sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最基本的实物义项。

senses.title: Put a force to work
senses.definition: to control and use a natural force for a purpose
senses.definitionCN: 为某种目的控制和利用自然力
senses.example: The dam harnesses the river.
senses.exampleCN: 大坝利用着这条河的力量。
senses.why: Straps that control a horse came to control power.
senses.whyCN: 控制马的皮带，变成了控制力量的手段。

senses.title: Strap an animal
senses.definition: to fasten a harness onto an animal
senses.definitionCN: 把马具系到牲畜身上
senses.example: They harnessed the horses at dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在黎明时给马套上马具。
senses.why: The noun of straps became the act of strapping.
senses.whyCN: 皮带的名词，转成了系皮带这个动作。

intro.en: Harness comes from Old French harneis, equipment for a horse or soldier.
intro.cn: harness 来自古法语 harneis，指马匹或士兵的装备。

items.en: Harneis meant military equipment.
items.cn: harneis 意为军事装备。

items.en: Harness named the gear of a horse.
items.cn: harness 指马的挽具。

items.en: The verb named putting on the gear.
items.cn: 动词义指给牲口套上挽具。

items.en: Harness extended to water and wind.
items.cn: harness 扩展到水力与风力。

items.en: It now names using any great power.
items.cn: 现在它指利用任何巨大的力量。

note.en: Harness is compared with look-alike words and with words for using power.
note.cn: 把 harness 与形近词以及表示利用力量的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Harness is leather on a horse, then leather on a river of power.
normalIntro.cn: harness 先是套在马身上的皮带，后来套在力量之河上。

normal.en: The horse wore a leather harness.
Wind farms harness the air.
normal.cn: 风电场利用空气的力量。

normal.en: We can harness sunlight for heat.
normal.cn: 我们可以利用阳光取暖。

normal.en: The climber wore a safety harness.
They harnessed the team to one goal.
normal.cn: 他们把团队的力量汇到一个目标上。

abstract.en: Power becomes useful only when it is held.
abstract.cn: 力量只有被握住，才有用处。

abstract.en: A wild river and a wild will both need a harness.
abstract.cn: 野河与野性，都需要一副挽具。

abstract.en: To harness is to listen to force before using it.
abstract.cn: 驾驭，是先听懂力量，再使用它。

examples.en: The farmer put the harness on the horse.
The dam harnesses the river.
examples.cn: 大坝利用着这条河的力量。

examples.en: They harnessed the horses at dawn.
examples.cn: 他们在黎明时给马套上马具。

dict_mnemonic.text: harness 本指马的「挽具」，把马系住才能干活，于是动词引申为「利用」自然力，如 harness solar energy 是利用太阳能；safety harness 是安全带。

root: 来自古法语 harneis（装备）；由给马套挽具，引申为控制并利用水力、风力、太阳能等巨大力量。

sensesIntro.en: Harness is gear for an animal, the use of a great force, or the act of strapping up.
sensesIntro.cn: harness 是牲畜的挽具、对巨大力量的利用，或套上挽具的动作。

core.en: Leather straps that hold a strong animal.
core.cn: 系住强壮牲畜的皮带。

branches.en: Buckled straps cross a horse's back.
branches.cn: 带扣的皮带横过马背。

branches.en: Water turns a wheel and lights a town.
branches.cn: 水推动轮子，点亮小镇。

branches.en: Hands buckle a collar before sunrise.
branches.cn: 日出前，双手扣上颈圈。

branches.en: The gear and the strapping are one action seen twice.
branches.cn: 挽具与套挽具，是同一动作的两种看法。

branches.en: To control a horse became to control a river.
branches.cn: 控制一匹马，变成了控制一条河。

intro.en: Harness takes plural and verb endings and forms gear compounds.
intro.cn: harness 加复数与动词词尾，并构成装备类复合词。

latinIntro.en: The word comes from Old French, not from Latin roots.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词来自古法语，并非拉丁词根。

items.example: The river is harnessed for power.
The team is back in harness.

items.exampleCN: 他们重新利用了老磨坊。

definition_zh: 严厉的；恶劣的；刺耳的；粗糙的
definition_en: unkind and severe, unpleasantly rough, or hard to live in
core_image: 砂纸般粗糙的表面划过指尖
scene: 冬天的风很刺骨。The winter wind was harsh.
sceneCN: 这里 harsh 是「恶劣的」（第 2 个义项）；句意：冬天的风很刺骨。

senses.title: Unkind and severe
senses.definition: cruel or unkind in words or treatment
senses.definitionCN: 言语或对待方式残酷、不仁慈
senses.example: He spoke in harsh words.
senses.exampleCN: 他说话很严厉。
senses.why: This is the social sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是人际层面的义项。

senses.title: Hard to live in
senses.definition: severe and difficult, as weather or conditions
senses.definitionCN: 指天气或条件严酷艰难
senses.example: The winter wind was harsh.
senses.exampleCN: 冬天的风很刺骨。
senses.why: A severe manner and severe weather share one word.
senses.whyCN: 严厉的态度与严酷的天气，共用一个词。

senses.title: Unpleasant to sense
senses.definition: unpleasantly strong or rough to hear or see
senses.definitionCN: 听或看时令人不适的强烈粗糙
senses.example: The harsh light hurt my eyes.
senses.exampleCN: 刺眼的光让我眼睛疼。
senses.why: Roughness is felt by the ear and the eye.
senses.whyCN: 粗糙也能被耳朵和眼睛感到。

senses.title: Rough to touch
senses.definition: rough and unpleasant to touch
senses.definitionCN: 触感粗粝不适
senses.example: The cloth felt harsh on the skin.
senses.exampleCN: 这布料贴在皮肤上很粗。
senses.why: This is the original texture sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最初的质地义项。

intro.en: Harsh probably comes from a Germanic root meaning rough or hairy.
intro.cn: harsh 可能来自意为粗糙、多毛的日耳曼语词根。

items.en: The root meant rough or hairy.
items.cn: 该词根意为粗糙或多毛。

items.en: Harsk described a rough surface.
items.cn: harsk 描述粗糙的表面。

items.en: Harsh described rough weather.
items.cn: harsh 描述恶劣的天气。

items.en: It also named severe words.
items.cn: 它也指严厉的言语。

items.en: It spread to light and sound.
items.cn: 它扩展到光线与声音。

note.en: Harsh is compared with look-alike words and with words for severity and roughness.
note.cn: 把 harsh 与形近词以及表示严厉和粗糙的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Harsh is a hand on sandpaper, a wind in a bare field, and a voice with no soft edge.
normalIntro.cn: harsh 是摸到砂纸的手，是刮过荒田的风，也是没有软边的声音。

normal.en: The judge gave a harsh punishment.
They live in harsh conditions.
normal.cn: 他们生活在恶劣的条件下。

normal.en: The harsh light washed out the photo.
normal.cn: 刺眼的光让照片失去层次。

normal.en: Do not use harsh words.
The cloth is harsh to the touch.

abstract.en: What is rough teaches the skin its limits.
abstract.cn: 粗糙的东西，教会皮肤它的极限。

abstract.en: A harsh word outlives its speaker's mood.
abstract.cn: 一句刻薄话，会比说话人的情绪活得久。

abstract.en: Hard conditions do not excuse hard hearts.
abstract.cn: 艰难的处境，不能为冷酷开脱。

examples.en: The winter wind was harsh.
He spoke in harsh words.
The harsh light hurt my eyes.

dict_mnemonic.text: harsh 本指触感「粗糙」，引申为言语「严厉」、天气条件「恶劣」、光线声音「刺耳刺眼」；harsh words 是严厉的话，harsh conditions 是恶劣的条件。

root: 可能来自意为粗糙、多毛的日耳曼语词根；由触觉上的粗粝，引申为言语的严厉、环境的严酷与感官上的刺人。

sensesIntro.en: Harsh describes unkind words, severe conditions, senses that sting, or a surface that scratches.
sensesIntro.cn: harsh 描述刻薄的话、严酷的条件、刺人的感官刺激，或刮手的表面。

core.en: A surface that scrapes the skin.
core.cn: 刮着皮肤的表面。

branches.en: A judge speaks without softening a word.
branches.cn: 法官说话一句也不软。

branches.en: Wind crosses a field with no shelter.
branches.cn: 风刮过没有遮挡的田野。

branches.en: Noon light makes everyone squint.
branches.cn: 正午的光让所有人眯眼。

branches.en: A hand pulls back from rough cloth.
branches.cn: 手从粗布上缩回。

branches.en: A hard climate can make hard manners.
branches.cn: 严酷的气候，会造出严厉的举止。

intro.en: Harsh takes comparison and builds an adverb and a noun.
intro.cn: harsh 加比较级，并构成副词与名词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root; the word is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词根，属于日耳曼语来源。

items.example: The harshness of the sun surprised us.
items.exampleCN: 阳光的强烈让我们吃惊。
这个计划遭到严厉批评。

definition_zh: 收获；收割；收成；（努力得到的）成果；采集（数据、细胞、野生资源）
definition_en: the act or season of gathering ripe crops, the crop gathered, the result of effort, or the act of collecting resources
core_image: 一片成熟麦田在短时间内被割倒、捆扎、装车，田里只剩整齐的茬
scene: 麦穗低下头，镰刀从田边推进，捆好的束子一列列码在车上，天色已近黄昏。The harvest must be brought in before the first storm.
sceneCN: 这里指「把成熟作物收回来」（第 1 个义项：收割庄稼）；句意为必须在第一场暴风雨前完成收获。

pos.zh: 收获；收割；收成；（努力的）成果
收割；采集（数据、细胞、野生资源）

derivatives.zh: harvest + -er（施动者或工具）→ 收割的人；收割机
harvest + -ing（动作名词）→ 收割作业；采集
harvest + -ed（过去分词作形容词）→ 已收割的
harvest + -able（能……的）→ 可收割的；可采集的
post-（之后）+ harvest → 收获后的（语义偏移：指采收之后的处理与储藏）
pre-（之前）+ harvest → 收获前的（语义偏移：指采收之前的田间管理）
harvest + man（人）→ 收割者；盲蛛（语义偏移：一种外形像长腿收割者的蛛形动物）

senses.title: Cut and gather ripe crops
senses.definition: to cut, pick or dig up ripe crops and bring them in
senses.definitionCN: 把成熟作物割下、摘下或挖出并运回
senses.example: They harvest the wheat before the rain breaks.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在雨来之前收割小麦。
senses.why: The oldest sense is the decisive act of the farming year: what has grown is finally taken.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项是农事年里决定性的动作：长成的东西终于被取走。

senses.title: The act or season of gathering
senses.definition: the work or the time of gathering crops, as in a late harvest
senses.definitionCN: 收集作物的劳作或时段，如晚收
senses.example: The harvest lasted three weeks that year.
senses.exampleCN: 那年的收获持续了三个星期。
senses.why: English often turns a season and its main activity into one noun, and harvest names both at once.
senses.whyCN: 英语常把一个季节与其主要活动合成一个名词，harvest 同时指两者。

senses.title: The crop that is gathered
senses.definition: the amount of crop produced and gathered in one season
senses.definitionCN: 一季中产出并收上来的作物总量
senses.example: A dry summer cut the harvest by a third.
senses.exampleCN: 干旱的夏天使收成减少了三分之一。
senses.why: By metonymy the act becomes the thing it produces, so people speak of a good or bad harvest.
senses.whyCN: 以转喻方式，行为变成它的产物，于是人们说收成好或坏。

senses.title: The fruit of long effort
senses.definition: the result or reward that comes from sustained work, as in the harvest of years of research
senses.definitionCN: 持续工作带来的结果或回报，如多年研究的成果
senses.example: The book was the harvest of ten quiet years.
senses.exampleCN: 这本书是十年静默工作的成果。
senses.why: The agricultural image generalizes: any long investment eventually has a gathering time.
senses.whyCN: 农业意象被一般化：任何长期投入最终都有采收的时候。

senses.title: Collect data in bulk
senses.definition: to gather large amounts of data or information, often automatically
senses.definitionCN: 大量收集数据或信息，常为自动进行
senses.example: The app harvests location data from every user.
senses.exampleCN: 这款应用从每位用户那里采集位置数据。
senses.why: Data is treated as a crop: it is already there, and the work is to gather it efficiently.
senses.whyCN: 数据被当作作物：它已经在那里，工作就是高效地把它收上来。

senses.title: Take cells or organs for use
senses.titleCN: 摘取细胞或器官供使用
senses.definition: to remove cells, tissue or organs from a body for medical treatment or research
senses.definitionCN: 从身体中取出细胞、组织或器官，用于治疗或研究
senses.example: Surgeons harvested a nerve from the patient's leg.
senses.exampleCN: 外科医生从病人腿部取出一段神经。
senses.why: The medical sense keeps the image of taking a living supply from where it grew.
senses.whyCN: 医学义保留了「从生长处取走活材料」的意象。

senses.title: Gather wild resources
senses.definition: to gather wild plants, shellfish or timber from their natural setting
senses.definitionCN: 从自然环境中采集野生植物、贝类或木材
senses.example: Villagers harvest shellfish at the low tide.
senses.exampleCN: 村民在退潮时采拾贝类。
senses.why: Not everything gathered is planted; the word also covers taking what the wild has produced.
senses.whyCN: 被收走的不都是种下的；这个词也涵盖取走野生环境产出之物。

senses.title: Autumn as the old season word
senses.definition: the season of autumn, the original meaning of the word in Old English
senses.definitionCN: 秋天这一季节，即该词在古英语中的本义
senses.example: In older texts harvest names the season, not only its work.
senses.exampleCN: 在较早的文本里，这个词指季节本身，而不只是季节里的活。
senses.why: Old English hærfest meant autumn; the modern crop sense narrowed out of the season when crops were cut.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 hærfest 意为秋天；现代作物义是从「收割作物的季节」中收窄出来的。

intro.en: Harvest goes back to Old English hærfest, autumn, from Proto-Germanic harbitas. The same word family survives as German Herbst, autumn. The crop sense narrowed out of the season sense. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: harvest 可上溯到古英语 hærfest「秋天」，源自原始日耳曼语 harbitas。同族词在德语中保留为 Herbst「秋天」。作物义是从季节义中收窄出来的。年代均为约数。

items.en: Hærfest named autumn and also the gathering of crops that filled that season; the two readings were not separated.
items.cn: hærfest 指秋天，也指填满这个季节的收作物；两种读法尚未分开。

items.en: The Germanic form harbitas is reconstructed from the older English and German evidence; it is not directly recorded.
items.cn: 日耳曼形式 harbitas 是由较早的英语与德语证据重构出来的，并未被直接记录。

items.en: The word is generally connected with a root meaning to gather or pluck, but the exact Indo-European form is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 这个词一般认为与表示「收集、采摘」的词根有关，但确切的印欧形式属重构。

items.en: Middle English kept both autumn and crop readings, while the season sense slowly passed to the Latin-derived word autumn.
items.cn: 中古英语同时保留「秋天」与「作物」两种读法，而季节义慢慢转给拉丁来源的 autumn。

items.en: The verb harvest appears later than the noun and extends the gathering image to data, organs and wild resources.
items.cn: 动词 harvest 比名词出现得晚，并把采集意象扩展到数据、器官与野生资源。

items.en: Source uncertain (deeper root): the pre-Germanic origin is reconstructed only, and no single Indo-European source is agreed.
items.cn: 来源不确定（更深词源）：日耳曼语之前的来源只有重构形式，学界并未达成单一印欧来源。

note.en: Group one holds words that look or sound close to harvest but name different things; group two holds words for taking in what has grown.
note.cn: 第一组是外形或读音接近 harvest、却指不同事物的词；第二组是表示「把长成之物收进来」的词。

entries.definition: The modern season word, borrowed from Latin autumnus; it replaced the season sense of harvest but is not related to it.
entries.definitionCN: 现代的季节词，借自拉丁 autumnus；它取代了 harvest 的季节义，但与之并非同源。

entries.definition: One who harvests or a machine that cuts and threshes grain; it is the doer, not the crop or the season.
entries.definitionCN: 收割的人或收割脱粒的机器；它是施动者，不是作物或季节。

entries.definition: A long-legged arachnid, named for its resemblance to a reaper; it is not a person who works in the fields.
entries.definitionCN: 一种长腿蛛形动物，因形似收割者而得名；并不是在田里劳作的人。

entries.definition: A celebration held after the crop is in; it marks the end of harvesting rather than the work itself.
entries.definitionCN: 庄稼收完后举行的庆祝；它标记收割结束，而非收割本身。

entries.definition: A plant or plant product grown in quantity; the harvest is the act of taking it in, or its total yield.
entries.definitionCN: 大量种植的植物或植物产品；harvest 是把它收进来的动作，或总产量。

entries.definition: The amount produced by land or by an effort; it is a quantity, while harvest can be the work, the season or the crop.
entries.definitionCN: 土地或努力产出的数量；它是量，而 harvest 可以是工作、季节或作物。

entries.definition: To cut grain by hand or machine; it is the first step of harvesting and does not cover data or organs.
entries.definitionCN: 用手或机器割谷；是收获的第一步，不涵盖数据或器官。

entries.definition: The general verb for bringing scattered things together; harvest is more specific and implies a crop ready to be taken.
entries.definitionCN: 把散落之物聚拢的普通动词；harvest 更具体，暗示作物已到可收之时。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Old English hærfest meant autumn: the season and its work were one word.
normal.cn: 古英语 hærfest 意为秋天：季节与季节里的活曾是同一个词。

normal.en: The family runs harvest, harvesting, harvester, harvested, harvestable.
Fixed phrases mark the field: bring in the harvest, harvest season, harvest festival.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出田间义：把庄稼收回来、收获季节、丰收节。

normal.en: The modern verb extends to data, organs, rainwater and shellfish.
normal.cn: 现代动词扩展到数据、器官、雨水与贝类。

normal.en: German Herbst still means autumn, the lost sense of the English word.
normal.cn: 德语 Herbst 仍指秋天，正是英语这个词丢失的义项。

abstract.en: Picture a field that disappears into stacks and sacks in a single afternoon.
abstract.cn: 想象一块田在一个下午里消失，变成一堆堆捆束与一袋袋粮食。

abstract.en: Picture a decade of notes finally tied into one bundle.
abstract.cn: 想象十年的笔记终于被扎成一捆。

abstract.en: Picture a tide pool emptied at low water, every shellfish taken before the sea returns.
abstract.cn: 想象退潮后的潮池被掏空，海水回来之前每一只贝都被取走。

examples.en: The combine harvested the field in two days.
examples.cn: 联合收割机两天就收完了这块田。

examples.en: This year's harvest was the smallest in a decade.
examples.cn: 今年的收成是十年来最少的。

examples.en: Researchers harvest tissue samples from consenting patients.
examples.cn: 研究人员从知情同意的病人身上采集组织样本。

dict_mnemonic.text: harvest 本指秋天，后来专指秋天里最要紧的活——把长熟的东西收回来；于是作物、收成、成果、数据都能「收」。

root: 古英语 hærfest「秋天」，源自原始日耳曼 harbitas；一般认为与表示「收集、采摘」的词根有关，但更早的印欧形式属重构。德语 Herbst「秋天」为同族词。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one moment: ripe growth is cut and carried in, and that moment then becomes a season, a yield, a reward and a way of collecting anything useful.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个时刻展开：成熟之物被割下并运回，这个时刻随后变成季节、产量、回报，以及收集任何有用之物的方式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ripe field is emptied in a short, decisive burst of work, and the year's growth becomes a store.
core.cn: 核心意象：成熟的田在一阵短促而决定性的劳作中被收空，一年的生长变成一座粮仓。

branches.en: THE ACT AND ITS TIME: cutting the crop and the weeks in which it is done.
branches.cn: 动作与其时间：割下作物，以及做这件事的那几周。

branches.en: THE SEASON AND ITS STORE: autumn and the amount it leaves behind.
branches.cn: 季节与其储藏：秋天，以及它留下的数量。

branches.en: THE REWARD: any long effort has a gathering day.
branches.cn: 回报：任何长期投入都有采收的一天。

branches.en: THE DATA FIELD: information is gathered like grain.
branches.cn: 数据之田：信息像谷物一样被收走。

branches.en: THE LIVING SUPPLY: cells, organs, shellfish and timber are taken from where they grew.
branches.cn: 活的供应：细胞、器官、贝类与木材都从生长处取走。

intro.en: Harvest is a native Germanic word, not a Latin derivative; its English family is built with ordinary suffixes and compounds.
intro.cn: harvest 是日耳曼本族词，并非拉丁派生词；它的英语词族由普通后缀与复合方式构成。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin relative exists for this word, so the Latin side is left empty; the family is entirely Germanic and English.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁同族词，因此拉丁部分留空；其词族完全属于日耳曼语与英语。

items.example: The noun once named the whole season.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词曾命名整个季节。

items.meaning: one who does, or a tool that does
items.example: The suffix builds harvester from the verb.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀由动词构成 harvester。

items.meaning: a reaper or a harvesting machine
items.example: The harvester cleared the last row at dusk.
items.exampleCN: 收割机在黄昏清完了最后一行。

items.example: The harvested grain was dried on racks.
items.exampleCN: 收下的谷子在架子上晾干。

items.meaning: ready or able to be gathered
items.example: Only half the stand was harvestable.
items.exampleCN: 只有一半的林分可采伐。

items.example: Postharvest losses were cut by better storage.
items.exampleCN: 更好的储藏减少了收获后的损失。

items.meaning: a reaper; also a long-legged arachnid

definition_zh: 危险；隐患；公害；冒险猜测
definition_en: something that could cause harm, or to risk a guess
core_image: 路面上被薄冰盖住的一道裂缝
scene: 湿滑的地面是个隐患。The wet floor is a hazard.
sceneCN: 这里 hazard 是「隐患」（第 1 个义项）；句意：湿滑的地面是个隐患。

senses.title: A source of danger
senses.definition: something that could cause harm or an accident
senses.definitionCN: 可能造成伤害或事故的事物
senses.example: The wet floor is a hazard.
senses.exampleCN: 湿滑的地面是个隐患。
senses.why: This is the everyday sense of a hidden risk.
senses.whyCN: 这是日常表示潜在危险的义项。

senses.title: Risk a guess
senses.definition: to say or try something without being sure
senses.definitionCN: 没有把握地说出或尝试某事
senses.example: He hazarded a guess.
senses.exampleCN: 他大胆猜了一下。
senses.why: The noun turns into the act of taking a chance.
senses.whyCN: 名词转化为冒险一试的行为。

senses.title: A public danger
senses.definition: a danger to health or safety in a place
senses.definitionCN: 某处对健康或安全的危害
senses.example: Smoke is a health hazard.
senses.exampleCN: 烟雾是健康危害。
senses.why: The risk becomes a named public problem.
senses.whyCN: 风险变成了被点名的公共问题。

intro.en: Hazard entered English through Old French as a dice game.
intro.cn: hazard 经古法语进入英语，最初指一种掷骰游戏。

items.en: The word may come from an Arabic word for dice.
items.cn: 这个词可能来自阿拉伯语中表示骰子的词。

items.en: Hasard named a game of dice.
items.cn: hasard 指一种掷骰游戏。

items.en: Hazard meant chance or luck in a game.
items.cn: hazard 指游戏中的偶然与运气。

items.en: Hazard shifted to mean danger or risk.
items.cn: hazard 转指危险或风险。

items.en: Hazard also named a source of harm.
items.cn: hazard 也指危害的来源。

note.en: Hazard is compared with look-alike words and with words for danger.

normalIntro.en: Hazard is harm waiting to happen.
normalIntro.cn: hazard 是随时可能发生的伤害。

normal.en: Wet floors are a hazard.
Smoke is a health hazard.
They cleared every fire hazard.
normal.cn: 他们清除了所有火灾隐患。

normal.en: He hazarded a guess.

abstract.en: A hazard is a shadow cast by a possible accident.
abstract.cn: 隐患，是可能事故投下的影子。

abstract.en: Name the hazard and it shrinks.
abstract.cn: 把隐患说出来，它就变小了。

abstract.en: Luck and hazard share one die.
abstract.cn: 运气与危险共用同一颗骰子。

examples.en: The wet floor is a hazard.
He hazarded a guess.
Smoke is a health hazard.

dict_mnemonic.text: hazard 是「危险、隐患」；health hazard 是健康危害，fire hazard 是火灾隐患，hazard a guess 是壮着胆子猜一猜。

sensesIntro.en: Hazard is a source of harm, a health danger, or the act of risking a guess.

items.meaning: a dice game, later a risk

items.exampleCN: 危险废物需要谨慎处理。

definition_zh: 危险的；可能造成伤害或损害的；由运气决定的（古义）
definition_en: dangerous or likely to cause harm, especially to health, safety or the environment
core_image: 一滩看不清底的不明液体摊在车间地面，旁边立着一块画有骷髅的黄色警示牌
scene: 车间地面上洇开一滩气味刺鼻的液体，班长伸手拦住刚进门的学徒，说 That puddle is hazardous, so nobody walks down this aisle until the spill team clears it.
sceneCN: 这里 hazardous 指「本身可能造成伤害或损害的」，取第 1 个义项（会直接伤人的危险）；句意为那滩液体有危险，在清理队处理干净之前谁都不许走这条通道。图中可辨识物件：警示牌、不明液体、防护靴、隔离栏。

pos.zh: 危险的；有危害的（作定语或表语，可与 to 连用说明受害对象）
（古义）由运气决定的、碰运气的

derivatives.zh: 危险地；以可能致害的方式
危险性；具有危害的属性

senses.title: Able to hurt the body
senses.definition: likely to cause injury to people who touch it, stand near it or work with it
senses.definitionCN: 人一旦接触、靠近或在其中作业就可能受伤的
senses.example: The broken railing made the whole stairwell hazardous for the workers.
senses.exampleCN: 断裂的栏杆让整个楼梯间对工人来说都变得危险。
senses.why: The base noun hazard names a source of harm, and the suffix -ous means full of, so the adjective describes something that carries harm inside it.
senses.whyCN: 本词由名词 hazard「危险源」加后缀 -ous「充满…的」构成，因此形容某物本身就带着伤人的因素。

senses.title: Harmful to health
senses.definition: having a harmful effect on the body when breathed in, swallowed or absorbed over time
senses.definitionCN: 经呼吸、吞咽或长期接触而对身体产生损害的
senses.example: Hazardous fumes from the old paint drifted through the whole building.
senses.exampleCN: 旧油漆散发的有害气体飘遍了整栋楼。
senses.why: The word is used where harm is not visible at once but accumulates, so health warnings attach it to smoke, dust and chemicals.
senses.whyCN: 这类危害往往不是立刻可见而是慢慢累积，因此健康警示常把该词与烟、粉尘和化学品连用。

senses.title: Harmful to the environment
senses.definition: able to damage water, soil, air or living things when released into nature
senses.definitionCN: 进入自然环境后会破坏水体、土壤、空气或生物的
senses.example: The label warns that the solvent is hazardous to aquatic life.
senses.exampleCN: 标签警示这种溶剂对水生生物有害。
senses.why: Environmental law extended the same word from the human body to the ecosystem, because the test is still whether something can be damaged.
senses.whyCN: 环境法规把这同一个词从人体扩展到生态系统，因为判断标准仍是某对象会不会被破坏。

senses.title: Dangerous conditions
senses.definition: describing roads, weather or working conditions in which accidents are likely
senses.definitionCN: 形容路面、天气或作业环境容易发生事故的
senses.example: Drivers were told to slow down in the hazardous fog.
senses.exampleCN: 司机被告知在危险的大雾中减速行驶。
senses.why: Here the danger comes from the situation rather than from an object, but the pattern stays the same: something in the setting can cause harm.
senses.whyCN: 此处危险来自处境而非物品，但构词逻辑不变：环境中有某样东西能造成伤害。

senses.title: Regulated dangerous goods
senses.definition: a legal label for goods that must be packed, labelled and transported under special rules
senses.definitionCN: 法规上指必须按特殊规则包装、标示和运输的货物
senses.example: Every container of hazardous cargo needs its own shipping document.
senses.exampleCN: 每一箱危险货物都需要单独的运输单据。
senses.why: Once authorities had to inspect shipments, the adjective became a category name, so it now appears on forms and labels rather than in description.
senses.whyCN: 当管理部门必须查验货运时，这个形容词就变成了分类名，于是它更多地出现在单据和标签上，而不是描写句里。

senses.title: A risky decision or guess
senses.definition: describing a step, assumption or investment that may fail badly
senses.definitionCN: 形容某一步骤、假设或投资可能带来严重后果的
senses.example: Betting the whole budget on one client was a hazardous move.
senses.exampleCN: 把全部预算押在一个客户身上是冒险之举。
senses.why: The old idea of a dice throw survives in this figurative use: the outcome is not controlled, and losing costs a lot.
senses.whyCN: 这一比喻保留了旧时掷骰子的意味：结果不受控制，一旦输了代价很大。

senses.title: Decided by chance
senses.definition: an older use meaning that something depends on luck rather than on plan or skill
senses.definitionCN: 旧用法，指某事成败取决于运气而非计划或技艺
senses.example: In older texts a hazardous voyage meant one whose end the sailors could not foresee.
senses.exampleCN: 在较早的文本里，hazardous voyage 指水手无法预知结局的航行。
senses.why: Hazard first named a game of dice, so anything hazardous was literally something the dice would settle.
senses.whyCN: hazard 最初指一种掷骰子的赌局，因此 hazardous 字面上就是「由骰子决定的事」。

senses.title: Explosive-atmosphere area
senses.titleCN: 防爆分区中的危险区域
senses.definition: a technical label for an area where flammable gas or dust may be present, so equipment must be certified
senses.definitionCN: 技术用语，指可能存在可燃气体或粉尘、因而设备须经认证的区域
senses.example: Only certified lamps may be fitted in a hazardous area of the refinery.
senses.exampleCN: 炼油厂的防爆危险区域内只能安装经过认证的灯具。
senses.why: Industrial safety turned the word into a zone classification, so a hazardous area is a mapped region rather than a described object.
senses.whyCN: 工业安全把这词变成了区域等级，因此 hazardous area 指划定的区域，而不是被描写的物体。

intro.en: Hazardous is the noun hazard plus the Latin-derived suffix -ous. Hazard itself came into English from Old French hasard, the name of a dice game, and is generally traced through Spanish to Arabic for the dice. The suffix is the regular Latin -osus, meaning full of.
intro.cn: hazardous 是名词 hazard 加拉丁来源的后缀 -ous 构成的。hazard 本身来自古法语 hasard，原是一种掷骰子赌局的名字，一般认为经西班牙语可追到阿拉伯语表示骰子的说法。后缀即常规的拉丁 -osus，意为「充满…的」。

items.en: Hasard named both a dice game and whatever the dice decided, so chance and risk were one idea from the start.
items.cn: hasard 既指掷骰子的赌局，也指骰子决定的结果，因此「偶然」与「风险」从一开始就是同一个概念。

items.en: Most dictionaries trace hasard through Spanish azar to Arabic az-zahr, the dice. This route is generally accepted, though the exact Arabic form behind it is still debated.
items.cn: 多数词典认为 hasard 经西班牙语 azar 追到阿拉伯语 az-zahr「骰子」。这条路径一般认为成立，但其后确切阿拉伯语形式仍有争论。

items.en: By the sixteenth century English hazard covered a risk taken in a game and then any source of possible loss or injury, which is the sense the adjective inherits.
items.cn: 到十六世纪，英语 hazard 已从赌局中承担的风险扩展到任何可能造成损失或伤害的来源，这正是形容词所继承的词义。

items.en: The suffix -ous descends from Latin -osus, full of or abounding in, as in dangerous and poisonous, so hazardous means full of hazard.
items.cn: 后缀 -ous 源自拉丁 -osus「充满…的、多…的」，如 dangerous 与 poisonous，因此 hazardous 意为「满是危险的」。

items.en: Source uncertain for the pre-Arabic origin of the dice word: its deeper etymology is unsettled and no Latin relative exists. Separately, only the first-recorded date of hazardous in English is uncertain; the French and Arabic route itself is not in dispute.
items.cn: 来源不确定：这个骰子词在阿拉伯语之前的更深来源没有定论，也没有拉丁同族词可援。另需区分：hazardous 最早的英语书证年代各家记载不一，这属于仅首见年代存疑；法语与阿拉伯语这条路径本身并无争议。

note.en: Group one holds words that look or sound close but do not all share the hazard root; group two holds near-synonyms that differ in how openly the danger shows.
note.cn: 第一组是形或音相近、但并非都含 hazard 词根的词；第二组是近义词，区别在于危险显露的程度。

entries.definition: The source noun meaning a thing or condition that may cause harm; the adjective only describes whatever carries it.
entries.definitionCN: 作为来源的名词，指可能造成伤害的事物或状况；形容词只用来描述带有这种危险的东西。

entries.definition: Built from hap, meaning chance, plus hazard: it describes something done without order or plan, not something dangerous.
entries.definitionCN: 由表示偶然的 hap 加 hazard 构成：形容做事没有条理或计划，而不是形容危险。

entries.definition: The nut tree and its light brown colour, from Old English hæsl; it has no etymological link with hazard.
entries.definitionCN: 指榛树及其浅褐色，来自古英语 hæsl；与 hazard 没有词源关系。

entries.definition: Thin mist or blurred air, probably a back-formation from hazy; its origin is separate and itself uncertain.
entries.definitionCN: 指薄雾或使空气模糊的状态，可能由 hazy 逆构而来；其来源与本词无关，本身亦不确定。

entries.definition: The everyday word for anything likely to cause harm; hazardous is its more technical and regulatory cousin.
entries.definitionCN: 最日常的说法，指任何可能造成伤害的事物；hazardous 是其更技术化、更常用于法规语境的说法。

entries.definition: Not meeting a safety standard, often said of equipment or premises; it judges compliance rather than innate harm.
entries.definitionCN: 不符合安全标准，多用于设备或场所；它评判的是合规性，而非事物本身的危害。

entries.definition: Highly dangerous in a dramatic, often life-threatening way; it is literary where hazardous is neutral and technical.
entries.definitionCN: 以戏剧化、常危及生命的方式极度危险；它偏文学，而 hazardous 中性且技术化。

entries.definition: Depending on chance or on a shaky support, so it may collapse; the emphasis is instability rather than toxicity or injury.
entries.definitionCN: 依靠偶然或不稳的支撑，因而可能垮掉；侧重不稳定，而不是毒性或伤害。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the real French and Arabic route, real fixed phrases and real compounds, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的法语与阿拉伯语来源、真实搭配与真实复合词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: hazard plus -ous equals full of danger, the same pattern as danger and dangerous.
normal.cn: hazard 加 -ous 就是「满是危险」，与 danger 变 dangerous 是同一套构词。

normal.en: The word began as a dice game, so hazardous still carries the flavour of a throw you cannot control.
normal.cn: 这个词最初是一场掷骰子的赌局，因此 hazardous 至今带着「掷出去就控制不了」的意味。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the fields: hazardous waste, hazardous material, hazardous cargo.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出使用领域：危险废物、危险物品、危险货物。

normal.en: The compound biohazard shows the same hazard element with a life-prefix.
normal.cn: 复合词 biohazard 展示了同一个 hazard 成分加上表示生命的词缀。

normal.en: Haphazard keeps hazard spelled the same but means unordered, a useful contrast to remember.
normal.cn: haphazard 拼写里保留同样的 hazard，意思却是「杂乱无章」，这个对照值得记住。

abstract.en: Picture a dice still rolling on the table: the number has not settled, and that unsettled state is the original hazard.
abstract.cn: 想象桌上还在转的骰子：点数尚未落定，这种悬而未决正是 hazard 的本义。

abstract.en: Picture a sealed drum with no label on it: nobody can see the harm inside, yet the harm is real.
abstract.cn: 想象一只没有标签的密封桶：里面的危害看不见，但危害确实存在。

abstract.en: Picture a yellow triangle standing where the floor looks perfectly dry, warning about what is not visible.
abstract.cn: 想象一块立在看起来完全干燥地面上的黄色三角牌，警示的正是看不见的东西。

examples.en: The old pipes were hazardous and had to be replaced within a month.
examples.cn: 这些旧管道有危险，必须在一个月内更换。

examples.en: Smoking indoors is hazardous to everyone in the room, not only the smoker.
examples.cn: 室内吸烟对房间里所有人都有害，不只是吸烟者本人。

examples.en: Investing there felt hazardous, but the returns were real.
examples.cn: 在那里投资让人觉得冒险，但回报是实实在在的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「害着得死」——害人的东西沾上就危险，于是 hazardous 就是危险的、有危害的

root: hazard（古法语 hasard「掷骰子赌局」，一般认为经西班牙语 azar 追到阿拉伯语 az-zahr「骰子」）+ 拉丁后缀 -ous「充满…的」；本义「满是风险的」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one line: something carries harm, and the harm spreads outward from the body to health, to the environment, to conditions, to regulated goods, to a risky decision, back to the old sense of chance, and finally to an industrial zone label.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一条线索展开：某物身上带着危害，这种危害从身体扩展到健康、环境、处境、受管制的货物、冒险的决定，再回到旧时的运气义，最后落到工业分区标签。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an unlabelled drum of liquid that can hurt whoever touches it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只没有标签的液体桶，谁碰到都可能受伤。

branches.en: THE BODY: the harm is immediate for the skin and slow for the lungs.
branches.cn: 身体：对皮肤是立刻的伤害，对肺则是缓慢的伤害。

branches.en: THE ECOSYSTEM: the same test moves from people to water, soil and fish.
branches.cn: 生态系统：同一套判断标准从人移到水体、土壤与鱼。

branches.en: CONDITIONS: weather and roads can carry harm without being objects.
branches.cn: 处境：天气与路面并非物品，却同样能带来危害。

branches.en: PAPERWORK AND ZONES: harm becomes a category on a shipping form and a colour on a factory map.
branches.cn: 单据与分区：危害变成运单上的一个类别和工厂图上的一个色块。

branches.en: CHANCE: the dice game survives as a risky decision and as the older sense of luck.
branches.cn: 偶然：掷骰子的赌局残留为冒险的决定，以及旧时的运气义。

intro.en: Hazardous can be read as the noun stem hazard plus the suffix -ous, and the same two pieces build several other English words.
intro.cn: hazardous 可拆成名词词干 hazard 与后缀 -ous，这两块还构成若干其他英语词。

latinIntro.en: The stem is French and ultimately Arabic, not Latin, but the suffix is genuinely Latin -osus. Latin contributed only the ending, so the Latin entries below are limited to that suffix.
latinIntro.cn: 词干来自法语并最终来自阿拉伯语，并非拉丁语，但后缀是真正的拉丁 -osus。拉丁语只贡献了词尾，因此下面的拉丁词条仅限于该后缀。

items.structure: hazard (noun stem, from Old French hasard)
items.example: The loose cable is a hazard for anyone passing.
items.exampleCN: 那根松脱的电缆对经过的人是个隐患。

items.structure: hasard (Old French source form, a dice game)
items.meaning: the original dice game and its chances
items.meaningCN: 原指掷骰子赌局及其偶然结果
items.example: The French word hasard still appears in histories of games.
items.exampleCN: 法语词 hasard 至今仍出现在博弈史著作中。

items.meaning: full of; having the quality of
items.example: A poisonous plant is full of poison in the same way.
items.exampleCN: 有毒的植物同样是以「充满毒」的方式构词。
那辆卡车危险地超载了。

items.example: Inspectors rated the site for its hazardousness.
items.exampleCN: 检查员评估了该场地的危险程度。

items.example: Nonhazardous waste goes to the ordinary landfill.
items.exampleCN: 非危险废物被送往普通填埋场。

items.example: Books were stacked in a haphazard pile.
The lab door carried a biohazard sign.
items.exampleCN: 实验室门上挂着生物危害标志。

latinEntries.example: It is the ending of Latin periculosus, full of danger.
latinEntries.exampleCN: 它是拉丁语 periculosus（充满危险的）中的词尾。

definition_zh: 大字标题；新闻标题；头条新闻；主演
definition_en: the title above a news report, a report important enough to lead the news, or to be the main performer
core_image: 报纸顶端一行又黑又粗的大字
scene: 这条新闻登上了头条。The news made the headline.
sceneCN: 这里 headline 是「头条新闻」（第 2 个义项）；句意：这条新闻登上了头条。

senses.title: The title of a report
senses.definition: the title printed in large letters above a news report
senses.definitionCN: 印在新闻报道上方的大字标题
senses.example: The headline was in large type.
senses.exampleCN: 那条标题用的是大号字。
senses.why: This is the basic printing sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是最基本的印刷义项。

senses.title: A leading news item
senses.definition: a report important enough to lead the news
senses.definitionCN: 重要到足以领衔新闻的报道
senses.example: The news made the headline.

intro.en: Heap forms a plural, adjective forms, and common phrases.
intro.cn: heap 有复数、形容词形式，也构成常见短语。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root; the word is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词根，属于日耳曼语来源。

items.example: A heap of sand stood there.
Heaps of leaves filled the yard.
items.exampleCN: 成堆的落叶填满了院子。

items.example: A heap of books lay there.
The plate was heaped with rice.
The bike went to the scrap heap.
items.exampleCN: 那辆自行车进了废料堆。

definition_en: to notice a sound, to be told news, or to listen to a case in court
core_image: 远处钟声传来，耳朵先于眼睛察觉
scene: 我听见远处传来钟声。I heard a bell in the distance.
sceneCN: 这里 hear 是「听见」（第 1 个义项）；句意：我听见远处传来钟声。

senses.title: Notice a sound
senses.definition: to notice a sound with your ears
senses.definitionCN: 用耳朵察觉到声音
senses.example: I heard a bell in the distance.
senses.exampleCN: 我听见远处传来钟声。
senses.why: This is the basic act of the ear.
senses.whyCN: 这是耳朵最基本的动作。

senses.title: Be told
senses.definition: to be told about something
senses.definitionCN: 被告知某事
senses.example: I hear she has moved away.
senses.exampleCN: 我听说她搬走了。
senses.why: The sound now carries news.
senses.whyCN: 声音在这里传递的是消息。

senses.title: Try a case
senses.definition: to listen to a case in a court of law
senses.definitionCN: 在法庭上听取案件
senses.example: The judge will hear the case today.
senses.exampleCN: 法官今天审理此案。
senses.why: A court listens before it decides.
senses.whyCN: 法庭先听，再作裁决。

intro.en: Hear comes from Old English hieran, to listen.
intro.cn: hear 来自古英语 hieran，意为听。

items.en: Hieran meant to listen or obey.
items.cn: hieran 意为听或听从。

items.en: Related words named the ear and hearing.
items.cn: 同源词表示耳朵与听觉。

items.en: Heren kept the sense of perceiving sound.
items.cn: 中古英语 heren 仍指察觉声音。

items.en: Hear also came to mean being told news.
items.cn: hear 也开始表示听到消息。

items.en: Courts hear a case before judging it.
items.cn: 法庭先审理案件，再作判决。

note.en: Hear is compared with look-alike words and with words for listening.
note.cn: 把 hear 与形近词以及表示听的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Hear is the ear opening, then the mind receiving news.
normalIntro.cn: hear 先是耳朵打开，然后是心里接到消息。

normal.en: I can hear the rain.
Did you hear the news?
I hope to hear from you soon.
normal.cn: 希望很快收到你的消息。

normal.en: Please hear me out.
The court will hear the case.

abstract.en: To hear is to let the world in.
abstract.cn: 听见，就是让世界进来。

abstract.en: The ear never closes, even in sleep.
abstract.cn: 耳朵从不关上，睡着了也一样。

abstract.en: Being heard is a kind of being held.
abstract.cn: 被听见，也是一种被接住。

examples.en: I heard a bell in the distance.
I hear she has moved away.
The judge will hear the case today.

dict_mnemonic.text: hear 是「听见」，消息进了耳朵就成了「听说」；法庭先把话听完，所以 hear 又表示「审理」。

root: 来自古英语 hieran（听、听从），与 ear 同源；由耳朵察觉声音，引申为接收消息，再用于法庭听取案件。

sensesIntro.en: Hear runs from a sound reaching the ear, to news reaching the mind, to a court listening to a case.
sensesIntro.cn: hear 从声音抵达耳朵，走到消息抵达心里，再走到法庭听取案件。

core.en: A bell ringing somewhere out of sight.
core.cn: 看不见的地方有钟在响。

branches.en: A bell reaches the ear.
branches.cn: 钟声传到耳朵里。

branches.en: A friend passes on the news.
branches.cn: 朋友把消息转告过来。

branches.en: A judge listens to both sides.
branches.cn: 法官听取双方陈述。

branches.en: A sound becomes a story.
branches.cn: 一个声音，变成一段故事。

branches.en: To judge well, one must hear fully.
branches.cn: 要判得公道，先听得完整。

intro.en: Hear takes verb endings and builds hearing, agent, and negative forms.
intro.cn: hear 加动词词尾，并构成听觉、施动者与否定形式。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root; the word is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词根，属于日耳曼语来源。

items.exampleCN: 我无意中听到了他们的谈话。

items.example: I hope to hear from you.
Did you hear about the fire?

definition_en: the quality of being hot, the act of making something hot, or strong excitement
core_image: 正午的柏油路面蒸腾出扭曲的热气
scene: 正午的太阳热得烫人。The heat of the noon sun was fierce.
sceneCN: 这里 heat 是「高温」（第 1 个义项）；句意：正午的太阳热得烫人。

senses.title: High temperature
senses.definition: the quality of being hot
senses.definitionCN: 物体或环境热的程度
senses.example: The heat of the noon sun was fierce.
senses.exampleCN: 正午的太阳热得烫人。
senses.why: This is the physical warmth itself.
senses.whyCN: 这是物理意义上的热。

senses.title: Make hot
senses.definition: to make something hot
senses.definitionCN: 使某物变热
senses.example: Heat the soup before serving.
senses.exampleCN: 上桌前把汤加热。
senses.why: The word turns from a state into an action.
senses.whyCN: 词性从状态变成了动作。

senses.title: Strong excitement
senses.definition: strong feeling or activity at its peak
senses.definitionCN: 情绪或活动最高涨的时刻
senses.example: He said it in the heat of the argument.
senses.exampleCN: 他在争论最激烈时说了那句话。
senses.why: Anger is described as fire.
senses.whyCN: 愤怒被比作火。

intro.en: Heat comes from Old English hætu, the state of being hot.
intro.cn: heat 来自古英语 hætu，意为热的状态。

items.en: Hætu named hotness or a hot season.
items.cn: hætu 指热或炎热的季节。

items.en: It shared a root with hot.
items.cn: 它与 hot 共用一个词根。

items.en: Hete kept the sense of high temperature.
items.cn: 中古英语 hete 仍指高温。

items.en: Heat became a verb meaning to make hot.
items.cn: heat 变成动词，表示加热。

items.en: The heat of an argument named its peak.
items.cn: 争论之热，指其最激烈的时刻。

note.en: Heat is compared with look-alike words and with words for warmth.
note.cn: 把 heat 与形近词以及表示温暖的词作比较。

entries.definition: how hot or cold something is

normalIntro.en: Heat is warmth you can measure, and anger you can feel.
normalIntro.cn: heat 是量得出来的热，也是感觉得到的怒火。

normal.en: The heat was hard to bear.
Heat the milk gently.
A heat wave hit the city.
The engine gives off heat.
In the heat of the moment, he quit.
normal.cn: 一时冲动之下，他辞职了。

abstract.en: Heat is motion hidden inside matter.
abstract.cn: 热，是藏在物质内部的运动。

abstract.en: Fire warms the hands and warns the eyes.
abstract.cn: 火暖手，也警告眼睛。

abstract.en: Anger is heat without a chimney.
abstract.cn: 愤怒，是没有烟囱的热。

examples.en: The heat of the noon sun was fierce.
Heat the soup before serving.
He said it in the heat of the argument.
examples.cn: 他在争论最激烈时说了那句话。

dict_mnemonic.text: heat 与 hot 同源，本指「热」；把东西弄热就是「加热」，情绪烧到最旺就是「激烈」，如 in the heat of 这一说法。

root: 来自古英语 hætu（热、炎热），与 hot 同源；由物理上的高温，引申出加热的动作，再比喻情绪或争斗的最高点。

sensesIntro.en: Heat is a hot state, the act of making hot, and the peak of strong feeling.
sensesIntro.cn: heat 是热的状态、加热的动作，以及强烈情绪的最高点。

core.en: Air shaking above hot asphalt.
core.cn: 滚烫柏油路上方颤动的空气。

branches.en: The pavement burns underfoot.
branches.cn: 路面烫着脚底。

branches.en: A pot steams on the stove.
branches.cn: 炉子上的锅冒着热气。

branches.en: Voices rise in a quarrel.
branches.cn: 争吵中声音越来越高。

branches.en: We add heat to cook, and cooking gives heat.
branches.cn: 我们加热来做饭，做饭又生出热。

branches.en: A heated talk can burn like a stove.
branches.cn: 激烈的谈话，能像炉子一样烫。

intro.en: Heat takes verb endings and builds tools, nouns, and new verbs.
intro.cn: heat 加动词词尾，并构成器具、名词与新动词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root; the word is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词根，属于日耳曼语来源。

items.exampleCN: 他们进行了一场激烈的辩论。

items.meaning: the system that warms a home

items.example: A heat wave lasted a week.

definition_en: in a heavy way, in large amounts, or to a serious degree
core_image: 雨点密集砸下，走路的人被压得弯下肩
scene: 雨下得很大。It was raining heavily.
sceneCN: 这里 heavily 是「大量地」（第 2 个义项）；句意：雨下得很大。

senses.title: With weight
senses.definition: in a way that shows weight or effort
senses.definitionCN: 显出重量或费力地
senses.example: He walked heavily up the stairs.
senses.exampleCN: 他脚步沉重地走上楼。
senses.why: The body carries weight here.
senses.whyCN: 这里身体承载着重量。

senses.title: In large amounts
senses.definition: in large amounts or with great force
senses.definitionCN: 数量很大或力度很强地
senses.example: It was raining heavily.
senses.exampleCN: 雨下得很大。
senses.why: Rain falls in heavy drops.
senses.whyCN: 雨以沉重的雨点落下。

senses.title: To a serious degree
senses.definition: to a great or serious degree
senses.definitionCN: 达到很大或严重的程度
senses.example: The town was heavily damaged by the flood.
senses.exampleCN: 这座镇子被洪水严重破坏。
senses.why: The effect presses down like a weight.
senses.whyCN: 影响像重量一样压下来。

intro.en: Heavily is heavy plus the adverb ending -ly.
intro.cn: heavily 由 heavy 加副词后缀 -ly 构成。

items.en: Hefig meant heavy or weighed down.
items.cn: hefig 意为重的、被压住的。

items.en: Hevy kept the sense of weight.
items.cn: 中古英语 hevy 仍指重量。

items.en: Heavily first described moving with weight.
items.cn: heavily 起初描写带着重量移动。

items.en: It widened to mean in large amounts.
items.cn: 词义扩展到数量很大。

items.en: It also came to mean seriously or greatly.
items.cn: 也表示严重地、在很大程度上。

note.en: Heavily is compared with look-alike words and with words for strong degree.
note.cn: 把 heavily 与形近词以及表示程度强的词作比较。

normalIntro.en: Heavily turns weight into a way of doing things.
normalIntro.cn: heavily 把重量变成了一种做事的方式。

normal.en: It rained heavily all night.
He was breathing heavily.
The area was heavily damaged.
She leaned heavily on the rail.
The plan was heavily criticized.
normal.cn: 这个计划受到严厉批评。

abstract.en: What falls heavily leaves a mark.
abstract.cn: 落得重的东西，会留下痕迹。

abstract.en: Rain can be loud without being angry.
abstract.cn: 雨可以下得很大，却并不愤怒。

abstract.en: Weight is a way of insisting.
abstract.cn: 重量，是一种坚持的方式。

examples.en: It was raining heavily.
He walked heavily up the stairs.
The town was heavily damaged by the flood.
examples.cn: 这座镇子被洪水严重破坏。

dict_mnemonic.text: heavily 是 heavy 加 -ly；步子沉是「沉重地」，雨下得猛是「大量地」，损失大是「严重地」，核心都是「重」。

root: 由 heavy（重的）加副词后缀 -ly 构成；heavy 来自古英语 hefig（重的、被压住的），因此 heavily 的核心义始终是「以重的分量」。

sensesIntro.en: Heavily applies the idea of weight to movement, amount, and seriousness.
sensesIntro.cn: heavily 把「重量」用在动作、数量和程度上。

core.en: Each step landing with full weight.
core.cn: 每一步都带着完整的重量落地。

branches.en: Boots fall slowly on the stairs.
branches.cn: 靴子在楼梯上慢慢落下。

branches.en: Rain drums on the roof.
branches.cn: 雨点敲打着屋顶。

branches.en: Walls crack after the flood.
branches.cn: 洪水过后，墙裂了。

branches.en: A heavy walk sounds like heavy rain.
branches.cn: 沉重的脚步，听起来像大雨。

branches.en: What falls heavily can hurt what it hits.
branches.cn: 落得重的东西，会伤到它砸中的东西。

intro.en: Heavily is built from heavy, which also forms nouns and comparisons.
intro.cn: heavily 由 heavy 构成，heavy 还能构成名词与比较级。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root; the word is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词根，属于日耳曼语来源。

items.example: He was heavily influenced by jazz.

definition_en: the back part of the foot, the raised part under the back of a shoe, or the position just behind someone
core_image: 走路时脚后跟先落地，鞋跟在地板上敲出声音
scene: 跑得太久，他的脚后跟磨出了水泡。After the long run, his heel had a blister.
sceneCN: 这里 heel 是「脚后跟」（第 1 个义项）；句意：跑得太久，他的脚后跟磨出了水泡。

senses.title: Back of the foot
senses.definition: the back part of the foot below the ankle
senses.definitionCN: 脚踝下方脚的后部
senses.example: After the long run, his heel had a blister.
senses.exampleCN: 跑得太久，他的脚后跟磨出了水泡。
senses.why: This is the body part.
senses.whyCN: 这是身体部位。

senses.title: Part of a shoe
senses.definition: the raised part under the back of a shoe
senses.definitionCN: 鞋底后部抬起的部分
senses.example: One heel of her shoe broke.
senses.exampleCN: 她一只鞋的鞋跟断了。
senses.why: The shoe copies the shape of the foot.
senses.whyCN: 鞋跟照着脚后跟的形状做。

senses.title: Close behind
senses.definition: the position just behind someone
senses.definitionCN: 紧跟在某人后面的位置
senses.example: The police were hot on his heels.
senses.exampleCN: 警察紧追在他后面。
senses.why: The follower is right at the back of the walker.
senses.whyCN: 追赶者正贴着走路人的后脚。

intro.en: Heel comes from Old English hela, the back of the foot.
intro.cn: heel 来自古英语 hela，指脚的后部。

items.en: Hela named the back of the foot.
items.cn: hela 指脚的后部。

items.en: Related words named the heel and the back.
items.cn: 同源词表示脚跟与后部。

items.en: Hele also named the shoe's back part.
items.cn: 中古英语 hele 也指鞋的后部。

items.en: At heel described a dog walking close behind.
items.cn: at heel 描写狗紧跟在脚边。

items.en: On the heels of came to mean right after.
items.cn: on the heels of 引申为紧接其后。

note.en: Heel is compared with look-alike words and with words for parts of the foot.
note.cn: 把 heel 与形近词以及表示脚部的词作比较。

entries.definition: one of the digits of the foot

normalIntro.en: Heel is the foot's back door, and the place a follower aims for.
normalIntro.cn: heel 是脚的后门，也是追赶者盯住的地方。

normal.en: My heel hurts after walking.
She wore high heels to the party.
normal.cn: 她穿高跟鞋去参加聚会。

normal.en: The dog walked at heel.
He fell head over heels in love.
A storm came on the heels of the heat.
normal.cn: 热浪之后紧接着来了暴风雨。

abstract.en: The heel is where a step begins.
abstract.cn: 脚后跟，是一步开始的地方。

abstract.en: What follows closely is said to be at the heels.
abstract.cn: 跟得紧的东西，就说在脚后跟处。

abstract.en: Even the back of a foot can lead.
abstract.cn: 就连脚的后部，也能带路。

examples.en: After the long run, his heel had a blister.
examples.cn: 跑得太久，他的脚后跟磨出了水泡。

examples.en: One heel of her shoe broke.
The police were hot on his heels.

dict_mnemonic.text: heel 是「脚后跟」，鞋照着脚做，所以也有「鞋跟」；跟在人后脚的位置，就是「紧随其后」，如 hot on the heels of。

root: 来自古英语 hela（脚后跟），属日耳曼语词；由身体部位引申为鞋跟，再由「跟在脚后」的位置引申出紧随其后的说法。

sensesIntro.en: Heel is the back of the foot, the shoe part that mirrors it, and the spot right behind a moving person.
sensesIntro.cn: heel 是脚的后部、照着它做的鞋跟，以及移动者正后方的位置。

core.en: A heel striking the floor first.
core.cn: 脚后跟先敲在地板上。

branches.en: The back of the foot touches ground.
branches.cn: 脚的后部触到地面。

branches.en: A shoe lifts at the back.
branches.cn: 鞋的后部被垫高。

branches.en: A runner follows close behind.
branches.cn: 追赶者紧跟在后。

branches.en: Shoes are shaped after the foot.
branches.cn: 鞋是照着脚的样子做的。

branches.en: To follow at the heel is to be very near.
branches.cn: 跟到脚后跟，就是离得非常近。

intro.en: Heel forms a plural and adjectives about shoes.
intro.cn: heel 有复数形式，也能构成与鞋跟有关的形容词。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root; the word is Germanic.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁词根，属于日耳曼语来源。

items.example: High heels are hard to walk in.
Rain came on the heels of the wind.

definition_en: the distance from bottom to top, how tall a person is, a high place, or the peak of something
core_image: 从地面垂直量到头顶的一条线
scene: 他的身高超过一米九。His height is over one metre ninety.
sceneCN: 这里 height 是「身高」（第 1 个义项）；句意：他的身高超过一米九。

senses.title: How tall
senses.definition: the distance from the bottom to the top of a person or thing
senses.definitionCN: 人或物从底部到顶部的距离
senses.example: His height is over one metre ninety.
senses.exampleCN: 他的身高超过一米九。
senses.why: This is a measurement.
senses.whyCN: 这是一个测量值。

senses.title: A high place
senses.definition: a high place or area of high ground
senses.definitionCN: 高的地方或高地区域
senses.example: The village sits at a height of two thousand metres.
senses.exampleCN: 这个村子坐落在两千米的高处。
senses.why: The measurement becomes a location.
senses.whyCN: 测量值在这里变成了地点。

senses.title: The peak
senses.definition: the strongest or highest point of something
senses.definitionCN: 某事物最强或最高的时刻
senses.example: The market was at its height in autumn.
senses.exampleCN: 市场在秋天达到顶峰。
senses.why: A tall thing reaches its top, and so does a trend.
senses.whyCN: 高的东西有顶端，趋势也有顶端。

intro.en: Height comes from Old English hiehþu, highness.
intro.cn: height 来自古英语 hiehþu，意为高的状态。

items.en: Hiehþu named being high.
items.cn: hiehþu 指高的状态。

items.en: It shared a root with high.
items.cn: 它与 high 共用一个词根。

items.en: Highthe kept the sense of tallness.
items.cn: 中古英语 highthe 仍指高度。

items.en: Height also named a high place.
items.cn: height 也开始指高处。

items.en: The height of a season meant its peak.
items.cn: 季节之 height 指它的顶点。

note.en: Height is compared with look-alike words and with words for vertical measure.
note.cn: 把 height 与形近词以及表示垂直高度的词作比较。

entries.definition: measuring a lot from bottom to top

normalIntro.en: Height measures up, then points to a high place, then to a peak in time.
normalIntro.cn: height 先向上量，再指向高处，最后指时间上的顶点。

normal.en: What is your height?
The tree grew to a great height.
We climbed to a height above the clouds.
normal.cn: 我们爬到了云层之上的高处。

normal.en: It happened at the height of summer.
Her fame was at its height then.
normal.cn: 那时她的名气正处顶峰。

abstract.en: Height is a line drawn by gravity's opposite.
abstract.cn: 高度，是逆着重力画出的一条线。

abstract.en: Every peak is also a place to fall from.
abstract.cn: 每个顶点，也是可以跌落的地方。

abstract.en: We measure height, but we feel depth.
abstract.cn: 我们量得出高度，却只能感受深度。

examples.en: His height is over one metre ninety.
The village sits at a height of two thousand metres.
examples.cn: 这个村子坐落在两千米的高处。

examples.en: The market was at its height in autumn.

dict_mnemonic.text: height 与 high 同源，核心是「高」；量出来是身高、高度，站上去是高处，到了最上面就是顶点，如盛夏与名气的顶峰。

root: 来自古英语 hiehþu（高的状态），与 high 同源；由垂直的测量值，引申为高处与高地，再引申为事物发展的高峰。

sensesIntro.en: Height is a measurement, a high place, or the strongest point of a thing.
sensesIntro.cn: height 是一个测量值、一处高地，或事物的最高点。

core.en: A straight line from floor to crown.
core.cn: 从地面到头顶的一条直线。

branches.en: A mark is made on the wall.
branches.cn: 墙上画下一道记号。

branches.en: A village rests far above the valley.
branches.cn: 村子远在山谷之上。

branches.en: The season reaches its warmest week.
branches.cn: 季节到了最热的一周。

branches.en: The measure becomes a place to stand.
branches.cn: 测量值成了可以站立的地方。

branches.en: A mountain top is a height in space and in time.
branches.cn: 山顶既是空间的高处，也是时间的高点。

intro.en: Height has a plural and builds a verb and related forms.
intro.cn: height 有复数形式，并能构成动词与相关形式。

latinIntro.en: The Latin root is altus, high, as in altitude.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词根是 altus（高），见于 altitude。

items.example: It was at the height of the storm.
items.exampleCN: 那正是暴风雨最猛的时候。

items.example: The town is busy at the height of summer.

latinEntries.example: The plane flew at high altitude.

definition_en: an aircraft with spinning blades on top that can rise straight up, or to carry someone by such an aircraft
core_image: 头顶巨大的旋翼高速旋转，机身垂直离开地面
scene: 救援直升机把伤员送下山。A rescue helicopter carried the injured man down the mountain.
sceneCN: 这里 helicopter 是「直升机」（第 1 个义项）；句意：救援直升机把伤员送下山。

senses.title: The aircraft
senses.definition: an aircraft with large spinning blades that can fly straight up
senses.definitionCN: 带大型旋转桨叶、能垂直起飞的飞行器
senses.example: A rescue helicopter carried the injured man down the mountain.
senses.exampleCN: 救援直升机把伤员送下山。
senses.why: This is the machine itself.
senses.whyCN: 这是机器本身。

senses.title: Carry by air
senses.definition: to carry someone or something by helicopter
senses.definitionCN: 用直升机运送人或物
senses.example: They helicoptered food to the flooded village.
senses.exampleCN: 他们用直升机把食物运到被淹的村子。
senses.why: The noun becomes the action of using it.
senses.whyCN: 名词在这里变成了使用它的动作。

intro.en: Helicopter joins Greek helix, spiral, and pteron, wing.
intro.cn: helicopter 由希腊语 helix（螺旋）与 pteron（翼）合成。

items.en: Helix meant a spiral.
items.cn: helix 意为螺旋。

items.en: Pteron meant a wing.
items.cn: pteron 意为翼。

items.en: Hélicoptère combined the two ideas.
items.cn: 法语 hélicoptère 把这两个意思合在一起。

items.en: Helicopter named the new flying machine.
items.cn: helicopter 成为这种新飞行器的名称。

items.en: The word became a verb meaning to fly someone out.
items.cn: 这个词又变成动词，表示用直升机运送。

note.en: Helicopter is compared with words sharing its heli- shape and with other aircraft words.
note.cn: 把 helicopter 与带 heli- 形式的词以及其他飞行器词作比较。

entries.definition: an informal word for a helicopter

normalIntro.en: Helicopter is a spiral wing that lifts straight up.
normalIntro.cn: helicopter 是一片能把机身垂直提起来的螺旋之翼。

normal.en: The helicopter landed on the roof.
They sent a helicopter to the island.
normal.cn: 他们派了一架直升机去岛上。

normal.en: The pilot flew the helicopter low.
normal.cn: 飞行员把直升机飞得很低。

normal.en: He was helicoptered to the hospital.
Helicopter parents watch every step.
normal.cn: 直升机父母盯着孩子的每一步。

abstract.en: A helicopter argues with gravity and wins.
abstract.cn: 直升机与重力争辩，并且赢了。

abstract.en: Its wing goes around so the body can go up.
abstract.cn: 翅膀绕圈，机身才能上升。

abstract.en: Some care hovers like a rotor, never landing.
abstract.cn: 有些关心像旋翼一样悬着，从不落地。

examples.en: A rescue helicopter carried the injured man down the mountain.
examples.cn: 救援直升机把伤员送下山。

examples.en: They helicoptered food to the flooded village.
examples.cn: 他们用直升机把食物运到被淹的村子。

examples.en: The helicopter landed on the roof.

dict_mnemonic.text: helicopter 拆开是「螺旋」加「翼」：靠头顶旋转的翼垂直升降；把它当动词用，就是用直升机把人或物运走。

root: 由希腊语 helix（螺旋）与 pteron（翼）经法语 hélicoptère 进入英语；命名依据是它头顶旋转的桨叶，后来也作动词表示用直升机运送。

sensesIntro.en: Helicopter names the rotor aircraft, and then the act of carrying someone by it.
sensesIntro.cn: helicopter 指这种旋翼飞行器，再指用它运送人的动作。

core.en: Blades spinning above a rising body.
core.cn: 旋翼在上升的机身上方飞转。

branches.en: The machine rises straight up.
branches.cn: 机器垂直升起。

branches.en: Supplies fly to a cut-off town.
branches.cn: 物资飞向与外界隔绝的城镇。

branches.en: A pilot hovers above the roof.
branches.cn: 飞行员在屋顶上方悬停。

branches.en: The aircraft becomes a flying ambulance.
branches.cn: 飞行器成了空中救护车。

branches.en: To helicopter someone out is to save time and lives.
branches.cn: 用直升机运人出去，是抢回时间与生命。

intro.en: Helicopter is built from Greek roots and forms verb endings.
intro.cn: helicopter 由希腊词根构成，并加动词词尾。

latinIntro.en: The roots are Greek, not Latin: helix and pteron.
latinIntro.cn: 它的词根是希腊语而非拉丁语：helix 与 pteron。

items.exampleCN: 他们用直升机把他运了出去。

items.meaning: the act of flying by helicopter
items.exampleCN: 用直升机运物资成本很高。

items.example: The helipad is on the roof.

items.exampleCN: 直升机机场去年启用了。
